T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.
T1110.detection_guidance: Monitor authentication logs for repeated failures against the same account followed by a success, especially from a single source in a short window.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.
T1078.detection_guidance: Correlate logins from previously unseen source IPs/geolocations with subsequent unusual activity from that account.

T1059.001.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
T1059.001.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution, often with encoded or obfuscated command-line arguments.
T1059.001.detection_guidance: Flag PowerShell processes with encoded (-enc) or obfuscated arguments, especially shortly after an anomalous login.

T1021.name: Remote Services
T1021.description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into a service specifically designed to accept remote connections, such as SMB, RDP, or SSH.
T1021.detection_guidance: Watch for a single account/device establishing connections to internal servers on service ports (445, 3389, 22) it does not normally touch.

T1046.name: Network Service Discovery
T1046.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation.
T1046.detection_guidance: Look for a single source connecting to many destination ports on the same host in a short time window with mostly rejected/refused connections.

T1071.001.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1071.001.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols such as HTTP/HTTPS to avoid detection by blending in with existing traffic.
T1071.001.detection_guidance: Correlate outbound HTTPS connections to rare/low-reputation destinations immediately following internal lateral movement or process anomalies.

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
T1041.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.
T1041.detection_guidance: Flag large outbound byte transfers to destinations already associated with a suspected C2 connection.

T1590.name: Gather Victim Network Information
T1590.description: Adversaries may gather information about the victim's networks that can be used during targeting.
T1590.detection_guidance: External scanning activity preceding any internal alert can provide useful reconnaissance context.
